descriptionChirho: The mandrake plant or its fruit (Mandragora officinarum), believed in the ancient Near East to promote fertility and love; consistently rendered across languages as a specific plant: spa 'mandragoras,' arb 'لُفَّاحِ' (luffah, mandrakes), kor '합환채' (love-fruit), swa 'matunda ya mapenzi' (fruits of love), hin 'दूदाइम' (dudaim). Covers all grammatical forms including construct chains, plural, and articular uses in the Rachel-Leah narrative (Gen 30) and Song of Songs.

A rare use of the same consonantal form translated as 'baskets' rather than 'mandrakes,' with strong multilingual convergence on a container meaning: eng 'baskets-of,' spa 'cestas-de' (baskets), arb 'سَلَّتَيْ' (dual baskets), kor '바구니' (basket), hin 'टोकरियाँ' (baskets). This likely reflects a homographic overlap or a distinct lexical entry that was clustered under the same lemma due to shared consonants d-w-d.
